framework.name: Slay-ILS-Designer
framework.title: Ontology-grounded RAG-enabled expert design framework for subsea inline structures
framework.description: Repository manifest for EDPR, EDES, EDAS, EDIKB, standard ILS layouts, validators, documents, and planned runtime pipeline tools.

EDPR.name: Engineering Design Problem Representation
EDPR.role: Converts a natural-language design request into APF/problem-map JSON with objectives, constraints, candidate solution families, retrieval needs, and evidence requirements.

EDES.name: Engineering Design Equipment Schema
EDES.role: Stores individual equipment and OAM part knowledge under the FBS-OAM framework.

EDAS.name: Engineering Design Assembly Schema
EDAS.role: Stores assembly-building knowledge, valid topology rules, interface logic, standard layout anchors, and FBS-OAM assembly structure guidance.

EDIKB.name: Engineering Design Intelligence Knowledge Base
EDIKB.role: Stores behavior knowledge graph nodes, numeric evidence rows, guidance nodes, uncertainty notes, feature-interaction candidates, and ML study candidates.

repo_review.summary: Core knowledge folders, schemas, validators, EDIKB graph, EDIKB dataset, EDPR prompts/specs, reference papers, and plotter/builder files are present. Pending items are EDPR examples and the three runtime pipeline scripts.
repo_review.json_parse_status: All discovered JSON files in schemas/, knowledge/edes/, knowledge/edas/, knowledge/edikb/, and framework_manifest.json parsed successfully during review.
naming_notes: Repository currently uses stable filenames without version suffixes, for example schemas/EDPR_METASCHEMA.json. Versioning should be carried inside the JSON metadata and this manifest.
Use EDPR consistently in filenames and code. The phrase EPDR appears to be a typo and should not be used for new files.
The existing folder name 'plotters and builders' is readable but less script-friendly than 'plotters_and_builders'. It can remain if scripts quote paths correctly.

edpr.role: Validated EDPR example problem JSON files
edpr.description: Place example EDPR JSON files here, including ILT L-branch strain minimization and inline valve no-roller-contact examples.

edas.description: Reusable ILS layout archetypes and anchors.

edikb.description: Consolidated numeric evidence dataset for quantitative comparison and ML-ready feature extraction.

tools.description: Planned retrieval helper. Given EDPR JSON, should load relevant EDES, EDAS, standard layout, EDIKB graph, and numeric dataset context.
Planned pipeline runner. Should parse natural-language problem text to EDPR JSON, validate it, and call retrieval.
Planned solution helper. Should use retrieved context to compare candidate ILS designs and produce an evidence-traceable recommendation.

runtime_sequence.name: read_manifest
runtime_sequence.action: Load framework_manifest.json first to discover schemas, prompts, knowledge sources, validators, examples, and pending tools.

runtime_sequence.name: parse_problem_to_edpr
runtime_sequence.action: Use knowledge/edpr/EDPR_PARSER_PROMPT_RUNTIME.md with user problem text and relevant framework context to emit EDPR JSON.

runtime_sequence.name: retrieve_context
runtime_sequence.action: Use tools/retrieve_context.py once available. Until then, manually load candidate EDES files, EDAS_SHARED_KNOWLEDGE.json, standard_ils_layouts.json, EDIKB_FULL_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH.json, and EDIKB_FULL_DATASET.csv according to EDPR retrieval targets.

runtime_sequence.name: reason_over_design_candidates
runtime_sequence.action: Use EDAS to check constructability/topology, EDES to understand component roles and constraints, EDIKB graph to reason over behavior, and EDIKB dataset for numeric evidence where available.

runtime_sequence.name: handle_feature_interactions
runtime_sequence.action: When a layout combines multiple components or subassemblies, check EDIKB for interaction nodes, numeric evidence rows, and ML candidates. Do not assume simple superposition unless evidence supports it.

runtime_sequence.name: solve_and_explain
runtime_sequence.action: Rank options against EDPR objectives and constraints, cite graph/dataset evidence, identify assumptions, and mark weakly supported conclusions as future study candidates.

llm_bootstrap_instructions: Use repository paths exactly as listed.
For problem solving, do not rely on EDPR alone. EDPR tells the system what the problem is and what to retrieve.
Use EDES for individual component knowledge.
Use EDAS for assembly construction, interfaces, layout anchors, and valid structural composition.
Use EDIKB graph for semantic behavior rules, guidance, uncertainty, and feature-interaction candidates.
Use EDIKB dataset for quantitative comparison when numeric evidence is needed.
If no reliable dataset supports a proposed comparison, state that the behavior is a future ML/FEA study candidate.
known_gaps_and_next_updates: Add knowledge/edpr/examples/ with validated example EDPR JSON files.
